From 8c88181ed452707f3815827225517b1964463b95 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Feb 2018 12:48:12 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: Sync kernel ABI header with tooling header for
 bpf_common.h

I recently fixed up a lot of commits that forgot to keep the tooling
headers in sync.  And then I forgot to do the same thing in commit
cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes"). Let correct
that before people notice ;-).

Lawrence did partly fix/sync this for bpf.h in commit d6d4f60c3a09
("bpf: add selftest for tcpbpf").

Fixes: cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes")
Signed-off-by: Jesper Dangaard Brouer <brouer@redhat.com>
Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>

diff --git a/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h b/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
index 18be90725ab0..ee97668bdadb 100644
--- a/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
+++ b/tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h
@@ -15,9 +15,10 @@
 
 /* ld/ldx fields */
 #define BPF_SIZE(code)  ((code) & 0x18)
-#define		BPF_W		0x00
-#define		BPF_H		0x08
-#define		BPF_B		0x10
+#define		BPF_W		0x00 /* 32-bit */
+#define		BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
+#define		BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */
+/* eBPF		BPF_DW		0x18    64-bit */
 #define BPF_MODE(code)  ((code) & 0xe0)
 #define		BPF_IMM		0x00
 #define		BPF_ABS		0x20
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `tools/include/uapi/linux/bpf_common.h`**
   - Added comments to the definitions of `BPF_W`, `BPF_H`, and `BPF_B` to clarify their sizes (32-bit, 16-bit, and 8-bit respectively).
   - Added a comment for the `BPF_DW` definition indicating it represents a 64-bit size, although the actual definition for `BPF_DW` (0x18) is commented out.

### Relationships
- The patch addresses a synchronization issue between the kernel ABI header and the tooling header for `bpf_common.h`, which was overlooked in a previous commit (cb5f7334d479). The modifications ensure that the comments in the tooling header accurately reflect the intended sizes of the BPF data types, thereby improving clarity and consistency across the codebase. This change is part of a broader effort to maintain alignment between different headers related to BPF.

bpf: Sync kernel ABI header with tooling header for
 bpf_common.h

I recently fixed up a lot of commits that forgot to keep the tooling
headers in sync.  And then I forgot to do the same thing in commit
cb5f7334d479 ("bpf: add comments to BPF ld/ldx sizes"). Let correct
that before people notice ;-).

Lawrence did partly fix/sync this for bpf.h in commit d6d4f60c3a09

Signed-off-by: Daniel Borkmann <daniel@iogearbox.net>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug was the failure to keep the tooling header (`bpf_common.h`) in sync with the kernel ABI header after a previous commit. This oversight led to inconsistencies in the definitions and comments related to BPF data types, which could cause confusion and potential errors in understanding the sizes of these types when used in BPF programs.

Here is the patch:
 /* ld/ldx fields */
 #define BPF_SIZE(code)  ((code) & 0x18)
-#define		BPF_W		0x00
-#define		BPF_H		0x08
-#define		BPF_B		0x10
+#define		BPF_W		0x00 /* 32-bit */
+#define		BPF_H		0x08 /* 16-bit */
+#define		BPF_B		0x10 /*  8-bit */
+/* eBPF		BPF_DW		0x18    64-bit */
 #define BPF_MODE(code)  ((code) & 0xe0)
 #define		BPF_IMM		0x00

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
#define BPF_W 0x00
#define BPF_H 0x08
#define BPF_B 0x10
```
Reason:
These definitions for BPF data types (word, half, byte) were not accompanied by comments explaining their sizes, leading to confusion about their intended use in BPF programs. This inconsistency arose from a failure to synchronize the tooling header with the kernel ABI header after a previous commit.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
#define BPF_W 0x00 /* 32-bit */
#define BPF_H 0x08 /* 16-bit */
#define BPF_B 0x10 /*  8-bit */
```
Reason:
The added comments clarify the sizes associated with each BPF data type, ensuring that developers understand the intended use of these definitions. This synchronization with the kernel ABI header helps prevent confusion and potential errors in BPF program implementations.
